context: Wilde to Leonard Smithers, Tuesday [? early October 1899], Hotel d'Alsace. Asking his publisher for four copies of The Importance of Being Earnest, published that February, to give away in Paris.
quote:
Hotel d’Alsace, Rue des Beaux Arts. Tuesday.

My dear Smithers, Would you, or could you let me have _four_ copies of my last play? I want to give them to some people here, who have been nice to me.

I enclose you a cutting from the Cri de Paris.

Ever O.W.
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2568, images 50-51 - one folded sheet, two sides written and the third blank. Emphasis: one underline, '_four_', flat and word-width. The volume italicises it and keeps it. Sixth confirmed case of a printed italic on an ordinary English word recording a real mark. 'Cri de Paris' is not underlined; the volume italicises it as a periodical. An annotation reading 'Forged' at the head of this letter, recorded but not endorsed. It is written in a bold dark hand quite unlike the light writing below it, across the top of side 1 above the address, with a separate cataloguer's mark in the top-left corner; confirmed at 5x with unsharp masking, and confirmed by Lovelle. The reading is not in doubt. Everything else about it is: whose hand, what date, on what grounds, and whether anyone acted on it. The Complete Letters print the letter as MS Texas with no note of a doubt, and Merlin Holland had the sheet in front of him. An unattributed annotation of unknown date does not outweigh the editor's judgement, so the letter is treated here as Wilde's and `marks_verified` is set on the underline of '_four_'. The annotation is recorded because it is on the document and the volume does not mention it - a reader who goes to Austin will see it, and should not have to discover it unprepared. If it is ever traced to a hand and a date, this entry is where the question starts: `manuscripts/hrc/2568-wilde-to-recipients-a-z/page-50-2554.jpg`.
